extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and students of literary philosophy (readers interested in imagination and principles of criticism)
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophical foundations and theses aimed at deducing the imagination and stating principles of production and 'genial' criticism in the fine arts; connects metaphysical claims about truth, subject/object identity, and primary intuitions to artistic creation and critical judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of a true philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: “It would at once explain and collect the fragments of truth scattered through systems apparently the most incongruous.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid system or critical account should both explain phenomena and gather dispersed truths from diverse, even conflicting systems. The text argues truth is widely diffused—often painted, masked, or mutilated—and deeper inquiry will reveal elements of truth in many schools; the good philosopher unifies these fragments rather than discarding them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis as method (unity from disparate doctrines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated by Synesius: separate doctrines (e.g., elements of Spinozism, Anima Mundi, mechanical Theism) when united yield a higher, coherent result (theism/Christianity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: in criticism or creative practice, seek to unite complementary insights from apparently opposed doctrines or techniques; anti-pattern: rigid sectarianism that excludes useful elements from other approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin from postulates / primary intuitions
rubrics_metrics.description: “In geometry the primary construction is not demonstrated, but postulated... Geometry therefore supplies philosophy with the example of a primary intuition, from which every science that lays claim to evidence must take its commencement.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt clear primitive assumptions or intuitions as starting-points for a theoretical system or for an aesthetic method. For creative production, recognize that some foundational constructive acts (primary intuitions) are accepted, not proven, and are necessary to generate subsequent forms. Anti-pattern: demanding complete derivation of every rule before using it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original constructive act of the inner sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy must proceed from 'the most original construction, and the first productive act for the inner sense'—the imagination must generate the primary line/idea prior to sensory images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the artist's original imaginative act that gives direction to inner sense. The text notes inner sense direction is largely an act of freedom; different persons have different degrees of inner sense (sensations only; forms and quantity; notions of things; reflections on reflections). Creative practice should cultivate this original inner constructive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance practical/moral and theoretical sides
rubrics_metrics.description: “The first principles must have a practical or moral, as well as a theoretical or speculative side.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic and critical principles should attend both to ethical/practical effects and to speculative/theoretical clarity. Productions that ignore the moral/practical dimension of reception or effect risk incompleteness; criticism should similarly not be purely abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful discipline-specific separation (avoid admixture)
rubrics_metrics.description: When working in a given science (or art), one must adhere strictly to its own principles and carefully exclude those belonging to the opposite science (e.g., natural philosopher avoiding subjective interpolations; transcendental philosopher avoiding objective interpolations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, preserve methodological purity appropriate to the chosen mode of artistic-criticism inquiry (e.g., avoid importing irrelevant explanatory devices). Anti-pattern: mixing incompatible explanatory vocabularies (e.g., forcing mechanical explanations into a purely introspective, imaginative account).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use austere and scientific scepticism as method
rubrics_metrics.description: “The means of separation is absolute scepticism... the comprehensive scepticism, which is aimed not against single prejudices but against the generality of prejudice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ disciplined, voluntary doubt (à la Descartes) to purge ingrained, natural prejudices that may obstruct insight. This is not shallow cynicism; it is a method to clarify foundational assumptions prior to constructing theory or criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve immediate realism of perception
rubrics_metrics.description: “The true and original realism... believes and requires neither more nor less than that the object which it beholds or presents to itself, is the real and very object.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In creative depiction and critical evaluation, respect the immediacy of perception—treat the object as the real object as perceived rather than an inferred phantom or mere representation. Anti-pattern: reducing experience to mere 'appearances' and losing the human immediacy that grounds artistic truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth must correlate with being
rubrics_metrics.description: THESIS I: “Truth is correlative to being. Knowledge without a correspondent reality is no knowledge; if we know, there must be somewhat known by us. To know is in its very essence a verb active.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works for whether their asserted truths correspond to some intelligible reality (psychological, moral, metaphysical) in the work; mere cleverness unmoored from being is not genuine knowledge. Emphasizes active knowing—creation and cognition as acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish immediate vs. mediate truth
rubrics_metrics.description: THESIS II: “All truth is either mediate, that is, derived from some other truth or truths; or immediate and original. The latter is absolute... the former is of dependent or conditional certainty.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a creative claim or critical proposition, note whether its truth-claims are immediate (self-grounded, absolute) or mediate (dependent). Immediate truths carry a different weight; be explicit about the epistemic status of assertions. Anti-pattern: treating derivative assertions as if they had absolute certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek a self-grounded (absolute) principle
rubrics_metrics.description: THESIS III: “We are to seek therefore for some absolute truth capable of communicating to other positions a certainty, which it has not itself borrowed; a truth self-grounded, unconditional, and known by its own light.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical and creative systems should aim to locate or embody a central, self-evident principle that confers certainty or coherence to subordinate elements. Practical: search for the core experiential or formal principle that renders parts meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness and non-object status of fundamental principle
rubrics_metrics.description: THESIS IV–V–VI: there can be but one such principle; it cannot be a thing/object (every thing is contingent); it is to be found in the identity of subject and object and 'manifests itself in the Sum or I am' (spirit, self, self-consciousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work's grounding principle should not be treated as merely another object in the world but as a unifying, self-manifesting act of subjectivity/ self-consciousness. For artists/critics: prioritize the living, self-duplicating act of consciousness (the 'I am') as the source of authentic artistic truth; anti-pattern: positing multiple equal ultimate principles or grounding art in mere objects without the living subjectivity that gives them meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligibility over complete demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: “The science of arithmetic furnishes instances, that a rule may be useful in practical application, and for the particular purpose may be sufficiently authenticated by the result, before it has itself been fully demonstrated. It is enough, if only it be rendered intelligible.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In production and criticism, a rule or principle may be pragmatically valid and useful even before it is formally proved; the test is intelligibility and effective application. Do not let the absence of formal proof paralyze practice; prefer clarity and usability. Anti-pattern: insisting on exhaustive theoretical demonstration before any application.
